samples.summary: A consumed `undoJumpTarget` is never cleared, so any `SheetView` remount replays a stale undo selection
samples.evidence: `undoJumpTarget` is only reset in `handleHistoryRestored` (document-detail.tsx:182); the consumption guard is the mount-local ref `lastHandledUndoJumpRequestIdRef` (sheet-view.tsx:244). `SheetView` is rendered conditionally in document-detail.tsx:744-769 — selecting a `datasource`/`lakehouse` tab (or a moment of `!ready || !activeTabId`) unmounts it, resetting that ref to 0. Switching back to the tab named by the still-set `undoJumpTarget` re-runs the effect at sheet-view.tsx:1443 with `requestId !== 0`, and `sheet.focusUndoSelection()` yanks the user's current selection to a long-past undo location. The change's own comment (document-detail.tsx:177-181) shows the author reasoned only about the history-restore remount.

samples.summary: A step that touches both row and column axis metadata resolves to no coordinates, and can hand the jump to an unrelated tab
samples.evidence: `resolveTab` only produces a header selection when `touch.rows.size > 0 && touch.columns.size === 0` (line 467) or the mirror at line 479. A single undo entry that carries both — e.g. a batch that writes `rowHeights` and `colWidths` (autofit after paste, an import batch: `setDimensionSize` is batchable, yorkie-store.ts:621) — falls through both branches and, absent cell ops, ends as `TabRank.Incidental` (line 510). `pickCandidate` then loses to any other touched tab that has coordinates, so undo both fails to select anything locally and switches the user to a different tab.

samples.summary: Pre-replay axis fallback can resolve cells to rows/columns that no longer exist after the replay
samples.evidence: `collectTouches` falls back to `beforeLookup` when a cell key is absent from the post-replay axes (lines 180-183). The comment at lines 141-146 justifies this only for tail truncation caused by an ordinary write. But undoing an *insert of rows at the end of the used range* is also a tail truncation — `diffAxisSpan` returns `undefined` for it (line 309), so the structural branch is skipped — and the removed cells then resolve against the stale pre-replay axis, producing a selection on rows that no longer exist in the sheet. `Sheet.applyUndoSelection` applies those raw coordinates unclamped (sheet.ts:5517).

samples.summary: `revealActiveCell` scrolls but does not re-prime the hidden cell input, unlike every other path that moves the selection
samples.evidence: Every keyboard/mouse path that relocates the active cell pairs `scrollIntoView()` with `primeCellInputForSelection()` (worksheet.ts:549-550, 4776-4777, 4793-4794). `revealActiveCell` (line 558-561), added for the undo path and called from `Spreadsheet.undo`/`redo` (spreadsheet.ts:655, 667) and `focusUndoSelection`, only scrolls — so after undo moves the selection the invisible cell-input overlay remains positioned over the previously active cell. The inline comment claims "The keyboard path does the same", which is true only of the scroll half.

samples.summary: `handleUndoJump` switches `activeTabId` without checking the target tab exists or renders a sheet
samples.evidence: `handleUndoJump` calls `setActiveTabId(selection.tabId)` unconditionally. `selection.tabId` comes from `root.sheets` keys (yorkie-store.ts:1346), which need not correspond to an entry in `root.tabs`/`root.tabOrder`; `activeTab` then resolves to `undefined` (line 669) and the default branch mounts `SheetView` on a tab with no metadata, while `TabBar` has no matching active tab. If the tab is of type `datasource`/`lakehouse`, `DataSourceView`/`LakehouseView` renders instead and the jump target is never consumed, leaving it pending to fire later (see the stale-target finding).

samples.summary: `diffRangeStyles` keys its multiset on `JSON.stringify(patch)`, which is property-order sensitive
samples.evidence: `tally` uses `JSON.stringify(patch)` as the identity key (line 346). Two structurally equal patches whose properties were inserted in a different order (the replayed clone versus the original) stringify differently, so both count as "changed" and the returned bounding range is wider than the region actually restyled. The result is only over-selection, not a wrong tab, hence nit.
